lesson.menu_desc: Distancing language: it is understood that / is thought to be / is reported to have -- saying only what you know when leadership wants answers now
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 21 -- Communicating Under Pressure -- Distancing language (it is understood that / is thought to / appears to have)
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fabiana Michelly Silva | Lesson 21 -- Communicating Under Pressure
lesson.grammar_point: distancing: impersonal passive reporting structures (it is thought that / is said to / is reported to have)
phases: When the Facts Are Not In

listenings.text: Thank you all for joining at short notice. I want to give you a holding statement now, and a fuller update at four o'clock. Here is what we know. It is understood that a fire broke out overnight at our contract manufacturer's plant in Penang. Nobody was hurt. The fire is reported to have started in the packaging area, and the main assembly line appears to have been untouched. That said, some of what I am about to share is still preliminary. The plant is thought to be closed for at least three days while the local authorities inspect it. There are unconfirmed reports that two of our pallets were damaged, and I would rather not speculate on the numbers until we have photos. What I can commit to is this: our buffer stock covers eleven days of hardware shipments to clients. It would appear that we have room, but not much. I will level with you: I do not have a firm recovery date yet, and I am not going to invent one. Next update at four.

Hi Fabiana, it's Marcus. I just came off the call with the executive committee, and I wanted to level with you before your four o'clock. First, the holding statement landed well. Nobody felt misled, and your composure on the bridge call was noticed. The distancing language helped: saying the plant is thought to be closed for three days, rather than it will be closed for three days, kept us from overpromising. Now the pressure. The committee wants a firm recovery date by tomorrow morning, and they are going to push you for one. My advice: hold the line. Buy time if you need to, but do not walk back what you said about the buffer. If someone asks you for a number off the record, treat it as on the record. Stick to your talking points: eleven days of buffer, a second supplier being qualified, and an update every twenty-four hours. One more thing: nobody expects you to be vague about the plan. Be careful about the facts, and firm about the actions. Call me after four.

extra_audio.text: Fabiana opens the bridge call with a short holding statement. She says it is understood that a fire broke out overnight at the plant in Penang, and that nobody was hurt. She explains that the fire is reported to have started in the packaging area. She adds that the damage to two pallets is still unconfirmed, and that she would rather not speculate. She commits to what she knows: eleven days of buffer stock. Finally, she promises a fuller update at four o'clock.

items.situation: A director asks: "Is the plant closed for a week?" The site manager has only told you "about three days".
tips: The plant is thought to be closed for about three days, but that is preliminary.
is thought to + base verb: the information comes from someone else.

items.situation: Someone in sales says twenty pallets were destroyed. You have seen evidence of two.
tips: Two pallets are reported to have been damaged. The figure of twenty is unconfirmed.
is reported to have + past participle: the event already happened.

items.situation: The CFO asks for an exact recovery date. You do not have one.
tips: I'd rather not speculate. I'll level with you: I don't have a firm date yet.
Be firm about what you do not know.

items.situation: A colleague asks for your estimate "off the record".
tips: I'm happy to share it, but please treat it as on the record: it would appear that we have eleven days of buffer.
It would appear that + clause softens a fact without hiding it.

items.situation: The committee wants you to promise the line will restart on Monday.
tips: The line is expected to restart early next week, and I will confirm at four.
is expected to: a forecast that belongs to the plan, not a promise from you.
